topic: Using end behavior and multiplicity to sketch polynomials
subtitle: Finding zeros and their multiplicity, reading end behavior from the leading term, and building a sketch from both

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct answer says the graph crosses at -3 and only touches at 1, and gives the reason from the exponents: the factor for -3 appears to the first power, an odd multiplicity, so the sign of the product changes there, while the factor for 1 is squared, an even multiplicity, so the sign does not change and the curve turns back. Naming which zero is which without the parity reason is half an answer.

problems.slot: (a) as x goes to minus infinity
(b) as x goes to plus infinity

problems.desc: Part (b): the sketch must show a curve that crosses the axis at -2, touches it at 1 without crossing, passes through the y-intercept at 2, falls to the lower left and rises to the upper right. Mark down any sketch that crosses at 1, since the squared factor there is the feature this item tests, and any sketch whose two ends point the same way, which would require an even degree.

problems.slot: (a) as x goes to minus infinity

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct description says the curve rises without bound on the left and falls without bound on the right, and names the two features that decide it: the degree is odd, so the two ends go opposite ways, and the leading coefficient is negative, so the right end is the falling one. An answer that names only the degree, or only the sign, has half the rule. The term 3x squared has no bearing on end behavior and should not be cited.

Part (b): the factored form is x squared times the difference of x and 2 times the sum of x and 2, so the sketch must cross at -2 and at 2 and touch at 0 without crossing, dip below the axis between -2 and 0 and again between 0 and 2, and rise on both outer ends because the degree is even with a positive leading coefficient. A sketch that crosses at 0, or that sends the two ends in opposite directions, misses the point of the item.

Part (b): with the leading coefficient equal to 1 the rule is the product of the square of the sum of x and 1 with the difference of x and 3. The sketch must touch the axis at -1 without crossing, cross at 3, pass through the y-intercept at -3, fall to the lower left and rise to the upper right, and the stated end behavior must match that. Reject a sketch that crosses at -1, and reject any end-behavior claim that does not follow from an odd degree with a positive leading coefficient.
